# Perform Park test for heteroscedasticity

<small>Source: [`man/performParkTest.Rd`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/man/performParkTest.Rd) · Help: `?performParkTest`</small>

Regresses the log of squared residuals on the log of a suspected variable.

## Usage

```r
performParkTest(model, data = NULL, variable)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   an object of class `lm`.

`data`
:   The data frame `model` was fitted to, or `NULL`, the default. The residuals and weights are read from the fit itself, and `variable` from the rows of `data` that hold the observations of the fit. Without `data` it is read from the model frame of `model`, which holds it only when it is a variable of the model under its own name (`x`, not `log(x)`); a model that transforms the variable needs `data`, as does a variable the model does not use. Since 0.16.0, data that are given are matched to the observations of the fit: rows with row names of their own by name, in any order; rows that only number themselves (a tibble, a data.table, a data frame whose row names were reset) by the row numbers of the fit, or in the order of the fit when they hold one row per observation. The rows the fit dropped may be there or not. Data whose rows cannot be shown to hold the observations of the fit are refused; see [`test_results`](test_results.md).

`variable`
:   name of the suspected explanatory variable.

## Value

An object of class `htest` containing the t statistic, p-value and degrees of freedom.

## Details

The slope coefficient from \(\log(e^2)\) regressed on \(\log x\) is tested for zero using a t statistic. A significant coefficient indicates scale depending on \(x\).

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, and `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit.
It refuses a multivariate `lm` ("needs a model with one response"), since 0.16.0; before, it stopped with a coercion error. An `mgcv::gam()` fit is tested as before 0.16.0, with smooth terms too, until a later step settles which tests take such a fit; since 0.16.0 its observations are matched to the rows of `data` by the row names of its model frame. Before, they were matched by position, since the residuals of a `gam` carry no names, and `data` with the rows of the fit in another order gave a wrong value.
Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in
[`test_results`](test_results.md), under *Supported models*.

## References

Park, R. E. (1966). Estimation with heteroscedastic error terms. *Econometrica*, 34(4), 888. [doi:10.2307/1910108](https://doi.org/10.2307/1910108)

## Examples

```r
 data(mtcars)
 m <- lm(mpg ~ wt + qsec, data = mtcars)
 performParkTest(m, mtcars, "wt")
```
